simple: every GPU trains a full copy of the model on a different part of the data, and the copies agree after every step.
analogy: every hall has the whole recipe book and reads a different part of the tasting notes.
precise: a training strategy in which N processes each hold a complete replica of the model, each computes the gradient of the loss on its shard of the global batch, the gradients are summed (all-reduce) and averaged, and every replica applies the identical optimizer update, so the replicas stay identical.
source: D1 of F8-12 (Shen Li et al., "PyTorch Distributed: Experiences on Accelerating Data Parallel Training", Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment, 2020 (tier 5; curriculum item 84). Sections on gradient bucketing, overlap and gradient averaging.); D2 of F8-12 (Alexander Sergeev, Mike Del Balso, "Horovod: fast and easy distributed deep learning in TensorFlow", 2018 (tier 5; curriculum item 85).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one complete copy of the model's parameters, kept by one process.
analogy: one hall's copy of the recipe book.
precise: the full parameter set (and, in plain data parallelism, the full gradient and optimizer state) held by one rank; correctness requires all replicas to hold the same values after each step.
source: D1 of F8-12 (Shen Li et al., "PyTorch Distributed: Experiences on Accelerating Data Parallel Training", Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment, 2020 (tier 5; curriculum item 84). Sections on gradient bucketing, overlap and gradient averaging.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: all the training examples used for one update, counted over all GPUs together.
analogy: the whole crate of tasting notes for one morning.
precise: the set of B samples whose mean loss gradient defines one optimizer step; with N ranks each rank processes a shard of B/N samples (the local or per-rank batch). Changing N while keeping the per-rank batch fixed changes B, and with it the optimisation.
source: D1 of F8-12 (Shen Li et al., "PyTorch Distributed: Experiences on Accelerating Data Parallel Training", Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment, 2020 (tier 5; curriculum item 84). Sections on gradient bucketing, overlap and gradient averaging.); D6 of F8-12 (Priya Goyal et al., "Accurate, Large Minibatch SGD: Training ImageNet in 1 Hour", 2017 (tier 5; not in the guide's registry, proposed in NOTES.md), used only for the statement that large global batches require retuning the learning rate.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a group of gradients that are sent together in one all-reduce.
analogy: one cart loaded with several pages of corrections.
precise: a contiguous group of parameter gradients, filled in the order the backward pass produces them, whose all-reduce is launched as soon as every gradient in it is ready; the bucket size trades the per-message cost (alpha) against how early communication can start.
source: D1 of F8-12 (Shen Li et al., "PyTorch Distributed: Experiences on Accelerating Data Parallel Training", Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment, 2020 (tier 5; curriculum item 84). Sections on gradient bucketing, overlap and gradient averaging.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: sending the first results while still computing the rest.
analogy: the carts leave with the first pages while the cooks write the next ones.
precise: running the gradient all-reduce of finished buckets concurrently with the backward computation of earlier layers (on a separate stream or with non-blocking collectives), so that only the communication that cannot be hidden ("exposed communication") adds to the step time.
source: D1 of F8-12 (Shen Li et al., "PyTorch Distributed: Experiences on Accelerating Data Parallel Training", Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment, 2020 (tier 5; curriculum item 84). Sections on gradient bucketing, overlap and gradient averaging.); D5 of F8-12 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard", chapter "Collective Communication", section on nonblocking collective operations (tier 1; curriculum item 77).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how close N GPUs come to being N times faster than one.
analogy: four halls finishing the work in a quarter of the time would be 100 %.
precise: for a fixed global batch, efficiency = T1 / (N × TN), where T is the time per step; for a fixed per-rank batch (weak scaling), efficiency = T1 / TN. Always state which one you report (milestone F3 asks for it).
source: M1 of F8-12 (Systems Curriculum (repository file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html), section 14.1 (rows "Overlap" and "Parallelism strategies") and milestones F3 and F6 (goal and acceptance tests quoted verbatim). A map, not a source for technical claims (AH-4).)

simple: splitting the numbers of one layer over several GPUs, so that each GPU computes part of every result.
analogy: every hall prepares its share of the vegetables for every bowl.
precise: intra-layer model parallelism: the weight matrices of a layer are partitioned across a group of N devices, each device computes the part of the layer's output that its partition determines, and collectives (all-reduce, or reduce-scatter and all-gather) combine the parts where the mathematics requires a sum or the whole tensor.
source: D1 of F8-13 (Mohammad Shoeybi, Mostofa Patwary, Raul Puri, Patrick LeGresley, Jared Casper, Bryan Catanzaro, "Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism", 2019 (tier 5; curriculum item 85): model-parallel MLP and self-attention, the f and g operators, placement within servers.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each GPU holds some columns of the weight matrix and computes the matching columns of the output.
analogy: each hall prepares its own eight vegetables.
precise: for Y = X A with A = [A0 … AN−1] split by columns, device r computes Yr = X Ar; the input X must be present on every device; the output is split by columns, and an element-wise function can be applied to each Yr without communication.
source: D1 of F8-13 (Mohammad Shoeybi, Mostofa Patwary, Raul Puri, Patrick LeGresley, Jared Casper, Bryan Catanzaro, "Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism", 2019 (tier 5; curriculum item 85): model-parallel MLP and self-attention, the f and g operators, placement within servers.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each GPU holds some rows of the weight matrix, multiplies its part of the input, and the GPUs add their results.
analogy: the four partial bowls poured together.
precise: for Z = Y B with B split by rows to match Y split by columns, device r computes the partial product Yr Br, and Z = Σr Yr Br is formed by an all-reduce (or a reduce-scatter if the next operation can work on a split result).
source: D1 of F8-13 (Mohammad Shoeybi, Mostofa Patwary, Raul Puri, Patrick LeGresley, Jared Casper, Bryan Catanzaro, "Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism", 2019 (tier 5; curriculum item 85): model-parallel MLP and self-attention, the f and g operators, placement within servers.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the set of GPUs that share the pieces of the same layers.
analogy: the halls that pour into the same bowl.
precise: the communicator over which a tensor-parallel layer's collectives run; in a job that also uses data and pipeline parallelism, every GPU belongs to one tensor-parallel group, one pipeline group and one data-parallel group, each a separate communicator.
source: D1 of F8-13 (Mohammad Shoeybi, Mostofa Patwary, Raul Puri, Patrick LeGresley, Jared Casper, Bryan Catanzaro, "Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism", 2019 (tier 5; curriculum item 85): model-parallel MLP and self-attention, the f and g operators, placement within servers.); D2 of F8-13 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard", chapter "Collective Communication" (all-reduce, reduce-scatter, all-gather) and chapter on groups and communicators (communicator splitting) (tier 1; curriculum item 77).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: putting different layers of the model on different GPUs and passing results from one to the next.
analogy: each hall does one course and passes the tray on.
precise: inter-layer model parallelism: the layers are partitioned into S consecutive stages, each on its own device (or group of devices); in the forward pass each stage receives activations from the previous stage and sends its outputs to the next; in the backward pass gradients flow the opposite way.
source: D1 of F8-14 (Yanping Huang et al., "GPipe: Efficient Training of Giant Neural Networks using Pipeline Parallelism", 2019 (tier 5; curriculum item 85): micro-batching, the bubble overhead, re-materialisation.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small piece of the batch that travels through the pipeline on its own.
analogy: one of Ayasha's eight smaller trays.
precise: one of M equal parts of a mini-batch; micro-batches enter the pipeline one after another so that different stages work on different micro-batches at the same time; their gradients are accumulated and the optimizer step is taken once, after all M (synchronous pipeline).
source: D1 of F8-14 (Yanping Huang et al., "GPipe: Efficient Training of Giant Neural Networks using Pipeline Parallelism", 2019 (tier 5; curriculum item 85): micro-batching, the bubble overhead, re-materialisation.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the time GPUs in a pipeline sit idle at the start and end of each step.
analogy: halls waiting while the first trays travel down the line and the last comments travel back.
precise: the idle time of the stages during the fill and drain phases of a synchronous pipeline schedule; for S equal stages and M micro-batches under the GPipe schedule, the bubble is the fraction (S − 1)/(M + S − 1) of the step time.
source: D1 of F8-14 (Yanping Huang et al., "GPipe: Efficient Training of Giant Neural Networks using Pipeline Parallelism", 2019 (tier 5; curriculum item 85): micro-batching, the bubble overhead, re-materialisation.); R1 of F8-14 (lab run of Listing 1 on pipe_sim.in: F8-14/pipe_sim.out, pipe_sim.log (g++ 13.3.0 with ASan and UBSan, exit code 0).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: every stage does all its forward passes first, then all its backward passes.
analogy: all trays go down the line before any comment comes back.
precise: the synchronous schedule of the GPipe paper: all M forward micro-batch steps, then all M backward steps, then one optimizer step; each stage holds the activations of all M micro-batches until their backward steps (unless it recomputes them).
source: D1 of F8-14 (Yanping Huang et al., "GPipe: Efficient Training of Giant Neural Networks using Pipeline Parallelism", 2019 (tier 5; curriculum item 85): micro-batching, the bubble overhead, re-materialisation.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: after a short warm-up, every stage alternates one forward and one backward pass.
analogy: a hall sends a comment back up the line as soon as it can, instead of waiting for all trays to pass.
precise: "one forward, one backward": stage s (counting from 0) first runs S − 1 − s forward steps (warm-up), then alternates forward and backward steps, then finishes the remaining backward steps; with equal stages it has the same bubble as GPipe but holds at most S − s micro-batches of activations instead of M.
source: D2 of F8-14 (Deepak Narayanan et al., "PipeDream: Generalized Pipeline Parallelism for DNN Training", SOSP 2019 (tier 5; not in the guide's registry, proposed in NOTES.md): the one-forward-one-backward schedule.); R1 of F8-14 (lab run of Listing 1 on pipe_sim.in: F8-14/pipe_sim.out, pipe_sim.log (g++ 13.3.0 with ASan and UBSan, exit code 0).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the results of the forward pass that a stage must keep until it does the backward pass.
analogy: trays kept on the hall's shelves until the guests' comments come back.
precise: the intermediate tensors saved during the forward pass of a micro-batch and needed by its backward pass; its size grows with the number of micro-batches in flight on the stage and with the micro-batch size, and it can be traded for computation by recomputing activations during backward.
source: D1 of F8-14 (Yanping Huang et al., "GPipe: Efficient Training of Giant Neural Networks using Pipeline Parallelism", 2019 (tier 5; curriculum item 85): micro-batching, the bubble overhead, re-materialisation.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: everything training keeps about the model itself: the weights, their gradients and the optimizer's notes.
analogy: the recipe book, tonight's corrections and the notebook of running notes.
precise: the parameters, the gradients and the optimizer state, as distinct from the activations (which depend on the batch) and temporary buffers; the ZeRO paper uses this term for the memory it partitions.
source: D1 of F8-15 (Samyam Rajbhandari, Jeff Rasley, Olatunji Ruwase, Yuxiong He, "ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models", SC 2020 (tier 5; curriculum item 85): model states, the three partitioning stages, their memory and communication.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the extra numbers an optimizer keeps for every weight between steps.
analogy: the two running notes for every recipe line.
precise: per-parameter tensors an optimizer carries from step to step; Adam keeps a first-moment (moving average of the gradient) and a second-moment (moving average of its square) estimate for every parameter, so two values per parameter, plus, in mixed-precision training, an FP32 master copy of the parameters.
source: D2 of F8-15 (Diederik P. Kingma, Jimmy Ba, "Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization", ICLR 2015 (tier 5; not in the guide's registry, proposed in NOTES.md): the two moment estimates and bias correction used in Listing 2.); D3 of F8-15 (Paulius Micikevicius et al., "Mixed Precision Training", ICLR 2018 (tier 5; not in the guide's registry, proposed in NOTES.md): FP16 computation with an FP32 master copy of the weights.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each data-parallel GPU keeps the optimizer state for only its own part of the weights.
analogy: each hall keeps only its own pages of the notebook.
precise: the optimizer state of P parameters is partitioned into N disjoint slices of P/N parameters across the N data-parallel ranks; each rank updates only its slice and the updated parameters are then all-gathered; the first of the ZeRO paper's three stages.
source: D1 of F8-15 (Samyam Rajbhandari, Jeff Rasley, Olatunji Ruwase, Yuxiong He, "ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models", SC 2020 (tier 5; curriculum item 85): model states, the three partitioning stages, their memory and communication.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: three levels of how much is split among the data-parallel GPUs.
analogy: first the notebook, then also tonight's corrections, then also the recipe book itself, read aloud page by page when needed.
precise: in the ZeRO paper's terms, partitioning of the optimizer states (Pos), additionally of the gradients (Pos+g), and additionally of the parameters (Pos+g+p); this course calls them stages 1, 2 and 3, as implementations commonly do.
source: D1 of F8-15 (Samyam Rajbhandari, Jeff Rasley, Olatunji Ruwase, Yuxiong He, "ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models", SC 2020 (tier 5; curriculum item 85): model states, the three partitioning stages, their memory and communication.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: add up everyone's arrays and give each rank only its own part of the sum.
analogy: passing bowls around the round table, each cook keeping only the bowl for their own pages.
precise: the collective that reduces N equal-length inputs element-wise and scatters the result in N equal blocks, block r to rank r; in MPI MPI_Reduce_scatter_block; with a ring, each rank sends (N − 1)/N of the data, half of an all-reduce (F8-02).
source: D4 of F8-15 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard", chapter "Collective Communication" (reduce-scatter, all-gather) (tier 1; curriculum item 77).); L1 of F8-15 (Open MPI 4.1.6 header in the build container (tier 4, opened): /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/openmpi/include/mpi.h lines 1759 (MPI_Reduce_scatter_block), 1331 (MPI_Allgather), 1345 (MPI_Allreduce).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a job that is still running but no longer makes progress, often without any error message.
analogy: the round table waiting for a bowl that never comes.
precise: a distributed job in which some processes block indefinitely, most often in a collective or receive whose matching operation on another rank will never be posted, because that rank is stopped, slow, deadlocked or on a different code path; no process exits, so exit-based failure detection does not trigger.
source: R4 of F8-16 (lab run hung (forensic evidence; watchdog off, 6 s time limit): F8-16/hung.out, hung.log (exit code 137, expected).)

simple: a timer that stops the job when an operation takes much longer than it should.
analogy: each cook's kitchen timer.
precise: a mechanism that bounds how long a rank waits for a communication operation; after the timeout it reports the stuck operation and aborts the job (or the communicator), turning a hang into a failure that a restart mechanism can handle. In Listing 1, the gradient all-reduce is started with MPI_Iallreduce and polled with MPI_Test; after watchdog seconds the rank calls MPI_Abort.
source: L1 of F8-16 (Open MPI 4.1.6 header in the build container (tier 4, opened): /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/openmpi/include/mpi.h lines 1306–1307 (MPI_ERRORS_ARE_FATAL, MPI_ERRORS_RETURN), 1324 (MPI_Abort), 1347 (MPI_Iallreduce), 1449 (MPI_Comm_set_errhandler), 1835 (MPI_Test).); R2 of F8-16 (lab runs ft_hang (rank 2 frozen at step 37) and ft_kill (rank 1 killed at step 23): F8-16/ft_hang.out, ft_kill.out with logs (exit code 0 after the restart).)

simple: stopping every process of the job at once, on purpose.
analogy: the alarm that stops the whole table.
precise: in MPI, MPI_Abort(comm, errorcode) makes a best attempt to terminate all tasks in the group of comm; Open MPI terminates all processes of the job and mpirun returns the error code. In NCCL, a communicator can be aborted so that pending operations stop and resources are released (unverified box).
source: D2 of F8-16 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard", version 3.1: sections on error handling and MPI_Abort, and on collective semantics (tier 1; curriculum item 77).); R2 of F8-16 (lab runs ft_hang (rank 2 frozen at step 37) and ft_kill (rank 1 killed at step 23): F8-16/ft_hang.out, ft_kill.out with logs (exit code 0 after the restart).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a saved state that is either completely old or completely new, never half-written.
analogy: the card written in ink and only then put in the safe.
precise: a checkpoint written to a temporary file, flushed to stable storage (fsync), and moved into place with rename, which POSIX specifies to replace the target atomically; readers verify size, a magic number and a checksum, and fall back to the previous checkpoint if the newest fails.
source: D3 of F8-16 (The Open Group, "The Open Group Base Specifications" (POSIX.1), entries rename and fsync (tier 1; not in the guide's registry by this title, proposed in NOTES.md).); R3 of F8-16 (lab run ft_corrupt (newest checkpoint cut to 100 bytes): F8-16/ft_corrupt.out, ft_corrupt.log (exit code 0).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: starting the job again from the last saved state instead of the beginning.
analogy: a fresh table starting from the card in the safe.
precise: a new instance of the job (often on new processes or new machines) that loads the newest valid checkpoint and continues from its recorded step; with deterministic data order and computation, the result equals that of an uninterrupted run.
source: R2 of F8-16 (lab runs ft_hang (rank 2 frozen at step 37) and ft_kill (rank 1 killed at step 23): F8-16/ft_hang.out, ft_kill.out with logs (exit code 0 after the restart).)

simple: putting a stopped job back in the queue so that it runs again later, possibly on other machines.
analogy: asking the booking office for another evening.
precise: a scheduler operation that returns a job that was running (or was stopped by preemption, failure or request) to the pending state under the same job identity; when it runs again it starts its batch script from the beginning, so the job itself must resume from its checkpoint.
source: D1 of F8-17 (SchedMD, Slurm documentation: sbatch, scontrol, the "Quick Start User Guide" and the GRES and preemption pages (tier 2; guide 4.5).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a signal the scheduler sends a short time before it stops a job, so that the job can save its work.
analogy: the knock on the door two minutes before the halls must be empty.
precise: a signal (commonly SIGTERM or a user-chosen one) delivered to the job's processes a configured time before the time limit or before preemption, followed by a forced kill if the job has not ended; the job's handler should checkpoint and exit.
source: D1 of F8-17 (SchedMD, Slurm documentation: sbatch, scontrol, the "Quick Start User Guide" and the GRES and preemption pages (tier 2; guide 4.5).); R2 of F8-17 (lab runs of Listing 4 alone (F8-17/worker.out) and of Listings 3 and 4 with a SIGTERM and a second run (F8-17/job_preempt.out, job_preempt.log; bash, no scheduler, exit code 0).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a process's number among the processes of the same job on the same machine.
analogy: a cook's seat number within one hall, not within the whole banquet.
precise: the rank of a process within the group of processes sharing a node; it is used to choose one GPU per process; in MPI it can be computed with MPI_Comm_split_type(…, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, …), and launchers also set it in the environment (Open MPI: OMPI_COMM_WORLD_LOCAL_RANK).
source: L1 of F8-17 (Open MPI 4.1.6 header in the build container (tier 4, opened): /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/openmpi/include/mpi.h lines 798 (MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED), 1461 (MPI_Comm_split_type).); R3 of F8-17 (lab run of Listing 5 on 8 processes: F8-17/local_rank.out, local_rank.log (Open MPI 4.1.6, exit code 0).)

simple: how often to save so that the time spent saving and the work lost to failures add up to as little as possible.
analogy: writing the card often enough, but not so often that writing takes the evening.
precise: for checkpoint cost C and mean time between failures M (with C much smaller than M), the interval T that minimises the expected overhead is approximately T* = √(2CM) (Young's first-order approximation); higher-order estimates refine it when C is not small next to M.
source: D2 of F8-17 (John W. Young, "A first order approximation to the optimum checkpoint interval", Communications of the ACM, 1974 (tier 5; not in the guide's registry, proposed in NOTES.md).); D3 of F8-17 (J. T. Daly, "A higher order estimate of the optimum checkpoint interval for restart dumps", Future Generation Computer Systems, 2006 (tier 5; not in the guide's registry, proposed in NOTES.md).); R1 of F8-17 (lab run of Listing 1 on ckpt_interval.in: F8-17/ckpt_interval.out, ckpt_interval.log (g++ 13.3.0 with ASan and UBSan, exit code 0; seed 12345).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
